2609.14157.title: When Tools Get in the Way: The Effect of Unnecessary Tool Availability on LLM Answering
2609.14157.paper_summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed with external tools that extend what they can do beyond their own knowledge. Tools help on tasks that need external information, but their availability may also change how a model handles questions that do not need them. Prior work has mostly asked whether models select and use tools appropriately; whether an unnecessary tool changes the correctness of answers has received less attention. We ask whether making a related but unnecessary tool available affects a model's ability to answer from its own knowledge, and whether a preceding tool interaction changes this behaviour. We construct 500 query pairs across 10 knowledge domains. Each pair consists of a tool query, which needs the domain's tool, and a closed-domain query, which does not. Six LLMs are evaluated with the tool unavailable, available, and available after a prior tool call. Across 3,000 baseline trials the pooled answer rate is 98.2%. When an unnecessary tool is available it falls to 63.5%, with large differences between models. The decrease occurs even when the tool is rarely called, so it cannot be explained by unnecessary tool invocation alone. A one-sentence scope-aware system instruction recovers most of the lost answers.
2609.14157.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLMs）越來越多地與外部工具一起使用，這些工具擴展了它們超越自身知識的能力。<lb/>工具幫助處理需要外部信息的任務，但它們的可用性也可能改變模型處理不需要外部信息的問題的方式。<lb/>先前的研究主要關注模型是否適當地選擇和使用工具；而不必要的工具是否會改變答案的正確性則受到的關注較少。<lb/>我們詢問提供一個相關但不必要的工具是否會影響模型從自身知識中回答的能力，以及先前的工具互動是否會改變這種行為。<lb/>我們在10個知識領域中構建了500對查詢。<lb/>每對查詢由一個需要該領域工具的工具查詢和一個不需要的封閉領域查詢組成。<lb/>在工具不可用、可用及在先前工具調用後可用的情況下，對六個LLMs進行評估。<lb/>在3000次基線試驗中，合併的回答率為98.2%。<lb/>當一個不必要的工具可用時，回答率下降至63.5%，不同模型之間存在較大差異。<lb/>即使該工具很少被調用，這一下降也會發生，因此不能僅用不必要的工具調用來解釋。<lb/>一條句子範圍感知的系統指令恢復了大部分丟失的答案。
